tagline: Oldham County horse country, with a turn for the river.
intro: From Goshen the byway follows US 42 northeast for nearly fifteen miles across Oldham County, a two-lane road in the hills between Interstate 71 and the Ohio River. Goshen is known for its thoroughbred breeding farms.

Partway along, KY 524 bends off to the river at Westport and comes back again, a small loop with a byway designation of its own. Hermitage Farm, a thoroughbred nursery whose main house is older than the Civil War, keeps its nearly 700 acres under easement so they stay farmland for good.

moments.title: Goshen
moments.text: Founded in 1849 as Saltillo, for the Mexican city near the Battle of Buena Vista, the town took the name Goshen, for the Bible's good soil, when its post office opened in 1851.

moments.title: Westport
moments.text: Out on the loop, a river town that kept a ferry to Indiana as early as 1800 and had steamboats calling at its docks before the railroad passed it by.
